Macrodontopteryx is classified as a genus of prehistoric pseudotooth birds, though its taxonomic validity is considered doubtful.
Due to uncertainty regarding its closest relatives, Macrodontopteryx is placed in the order Odontopterygiformes, suggesting it may be related to pelicans, storks, or waterfowl.
Macrodontopteryx is classified within the family Pelagornithidae.
The genus status is disputed, with some researchers suggesting it may not be a distinct genus but rather a large member of the genus Odontopteryx or a young specimen of Dasornis.
Macrodontopteryx lived during the Ypresian to Lutetian stages, spanning from 56 to 41.03 million years ago.
It is debated whether the fossil Proceriavis martini belongs to Macrodontopteryx, as the 20-million-year age difference between the specimens makes a synonymy highly uncertain.
Recent analysis suggests that the material previously referred to as Proceriavis may actually belong to a ratite bird rather than a pseudotooth bird.
